blocks.heading: What this section covers
blocks.text: Identify the conditions of supply, and show how a change in one shifts the supply curve.

blocks.heading: The conditions of supply
blocks.text: The conditions of supply are the influences on supply other than the good's own price. The list to know: the costs of the inputs used to make the good; the technology of production; indirect taxes on the good and subsidies for producing it; the prices of other goods the producer could make instead; the weather, for farm and fishing goods; and the number of sellers. The good's own price stays off the list, because it moves the market along the curve.

blocks.heading: A cost fall shifts the curve
blocks.text: Start with a condition: the price of vinyl falls for Namib Signs, a sign-painting firm in Windhoek, while its price per sign stays at N$150. Because printing becomes cheaper at each price, this causes the firm to offer more signs at N$150 - 60 a month instead of 40. The whole supply curve shifts right: an increase in supply, meaning more is offered at every price. A rise in an input cost would shift it left: a decrease in supply.

blocks.heading: Weather on the harvest
blocks.text: The weather is a condition of supply for farm goods. Good rains round Otavi raise the maize offered at each price; drought shrinks it, shifting the curve left. Rice farmers in Vietnam watch the same condition: a strong Mekong delta harvest shifts their market's supply curve right, a weak one left. In each case the good's own price has not changed - the whole relationship between price and quantity has.

blocks.heading: Movement or shift
blocks.text: The confusion learners make: a price change and a condition change are both written as "supply changed". The boundary: the good's own price moves the market along the curve; a condition of supply, with the price unchanged, shifts the whole curve. The test: whether the good's own price changed. Where it did, the diagram shows an extension or a contraction along the curve; where it did not, a shift.

blocks.heading: Connections
blocks.text: Topic 2.5 traces what these shifts do to the market price, and topic 2.6 asks how strongly quantity supplied responds to price.
